source.title: When Bad Data Leads to Good Models
source.authors: Kenneth Li; Yida Chen; Fernanda Viégas; M. Wattenberg

record.tranche_reason: The study uses toy transformers and probe-based measurements to test whether feature-data frequency relates to representation entanglement, rather than reproducing the original study's full method.
record.gate_note: Rows record the toy-model entanglement sweep and the Olmo-1B toxicity-probe comparison. The detoxification, generation-toxicity, capability, and jailbreak results do not measure the claim versions. Probe settings and verbalized-token counts are not separate geometry results; the paper cites the superposition hypothesis but those citations are not rows.
record.test_reason: The toy experiment trains 4-layer transformers with 12 Markov-chain 'features' in a 4-D residual stream, more features than dimensions. It measures how one feature's superposition entanglement (max |cos|) changes with its training frequency. That is a new setting with a result on V1. The Olmo-1B part measures only toxicity-probe accuracy, not superposition, so it does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one correction. The authors say toxic data yields a 'less entangled' toxicity representation in Olmo-1B, but they measure only probe accuracy there, not entanglement. Their other conclusions: such models are easier to detoxify via ITI, prompting, SFT and DPO with little capability cost, and steerability declines beyond about 10% toxic data.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it builds on Elhage et al.'s superposition framework. It varies the training frequency of one feature and measures maximum absolute cosine similarity of probe-derived directions in a toy transformer; it also applies linear probes to toxicity in Olmo-1B.
record.method_sensitivity: Toy-model entanglement changes with the underrepresented feature's training-data frequency. In Olmo-1B, the paper compares C4-only training with C4 plus 25% 4chan for the reported probe result.

fits_no_version.finding: In Olmo-1B, adding 25% 4chan data to C4 pretraining raised average toxicity-probe validation accuracy across attention heads (p=0.0002) and produced a fatter right tail of high-accuracy heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher pretraining frequency of a concept yields a more linearly separable, more head-localized representation of it in LLMs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267 (2025)
record.problems: The toy-model entanglement values are shown only in Figure 3, with no exact plotted values available in the text. The LLM probe comparison is between C4-only and 25% 4chan rather than a reported sweep of probe accuracies across all toxic-data proportions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows were left out.

untested.parts: Sparsity-dependent phase transition as defined via feature sparsity. Regular or polytope geometry. Near-orthogonality of the superposed directions.
All. Polysemantic neurons and capacity allocation are not examined.
All. No neuron-level distribution or SAE analysis in Olmo-1B.

missing.what: The paper states a Welch-bound minimum average entanglement of 0.43 for N=12, M=4, versus an observed natural entanglement of ~0.8. This means learned features are far from the evenly spread arrangement, which bears on V1's regular-geometry part.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The toy 'features' are unique Markov-chain sequences rather than sparse synthetic features, so this is an adjacent test of V1. Detoxification, capability and GCG results do not bear on any version. The tranche was changed from T2 to T3: the setting is new and the question (frequency vs entanglement) differs from the original's.

versions.untested_parts: The toy experiment varies feature data frequency, not co-activation sparsity; it does not test a sparsity-dependent transition or establish regular geometry.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from limited capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The LLM experiment probes toxicity in attention-head activations; it does not test SAE recovery or characterize feature distributions across neurons generally.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study defines feature directions for its measurements but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: 4-layer transformer (toy)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the maximum absolute cosine similarity between the underrepresented feature direction and other feature directions while varying its chain's share of training data.

conditions.value: increased across data compositions; exact proportions not stated

rows.baseline: Natural entanglement for compressing features into a 4-dimensional residual stream is around 0.8
rows.note: The text reports that entanglement drops as the underrepresented feature's data increases, approaching the average entanglement of the other features. The plotted values are not available in the text.
rows.check: Link kept. The manipulated variable is training-data frequency of Markov-chain sequences, not activation sparsity of features, so the match to V1's sparsity-dependent transition is loose. Values are figure-only. The authors describe a 'sharp drop' toward the other features' average.

rows.subject: Olmo-1B
rows.size_stated: 1B; hidden size 1024; 24 layers; 16 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Fit binary linear toxicity classifiers on each attention head's last-token activations and compared validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Difference in average toxicity-probe validation accuracy across heads and layers
rows.value: The toxicity-trained model's average accuracy was higher; 95% confidence interval for the difference: [0.67, 1.18]
rows.note: The text also describes a fatter right tail of probe accuracies and more attention heads specializing in toxicity; it does not give the absolute mean accuracies.
rows.check: Higher toxicity-probe validation accuracy across attention heads measures linear separability of one concept. It does not show features spread across many neurons, does not involve SAE recovery, and entanglement is never measured in Olmo. It does not bear on V4. The CI units [0.67, 1.18] are unstated (likely percentage points). Single comparison: C4 vs C4+25% 4chan.

relationships.condition: 4-layer toy transformer, 4-D residual stream, 12 Markov-chain sequence features, 10 seeds, varying one chain's data share
relationships.reason: Features are superposed (entanglement ~0.8). An underrepresented feature's entanglement drops as its frequency rises, approaching the other features' average (r1, r2). This fits frequency-dependent allocation in superposition. Values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Features were superposed, with entanglement around 0.8, and an underrepresented feature's entanglement dropped toward the other features' average as its frequency rose. This fits frequency-dependent allocation in superposition.
